instruction: Add a sheet named 'Analysis', merge A1:D1 for 'Financial Overview', merge A2:B2 for 'Investment Type', and merge C2:D2 for 'Return Period'.

metadata.explanation: This variation requires creating a new sheet named 'Analysis' with a different header structure. The task involves merging A1:D1 for 'Financial Overview' header, and two merged cells in row 2: A2:B2 for 'Investment Type' and C2:D2 for 'Return Period'. The evaluator checks sheet existence, cell values, and merge status for all specified cells. Custom getter extracts sheet structure including merged cell ranges, and custom metric validates each cell against expected configuration.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Partial credit: Each cell check contributes 1/10 of total score. Full score requires all 10 checks to pass (sheet exists, correct values in A1/A2/C2, correct merge status for all cells).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: sheet creation, cell merging, and cell values
Merge status check uses proper coordinate parsing with _is_coord_in_range helper function (metrics/calc.py:5-34)
The helper function correctly parses coordinates using openpyxl utilities (coordinate_from_string, column_index_from_string)
Boundary checking is semantically correct: checks if coord is within range using row/column index comparison
Cell value verification uses exact string matching which is appropriate for the task
Expected configuration has complete coverage: checks sheet name, 3 cell values, 7 merge statuses, and 2 boundary checks (E1, E2 not merged)
Postconfig properly saves the file with Ctrl+S to ensure state persistence before verification
Partial credit scoring is logical: 10 individual checks, each contributing 1/10 of the total score
Getter correctly extracts sheet structure using openpyxl, reading both cell values and merged cell ranges
Data flow is correct: getter extracts merged ranges as strings → metric parses them → checks if cells fall within ranges
